card.name: Linking words before severe outcomes
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as for, to, of, including and or that come right before a severe outcome like severe COVID-19, seizures, death, dehydration or severe OHSS. The next word is usually a serious complication.

modes.label: Link before severe outcome
modes.description: A preposition or verb leading into a named serious complication or progression.
modes.example: who are at high risk<< for>> progression to severe COVID-19,

modes.label: Leading to harm
modes.description: The word "to" or "of" after leading or signs, ahead of seizures, coma, death or dehydration.
modes.example: Severe hyponatremia can be life-threatening if it is not promptly diagnosed and treated, leading<< to>> seizures, coma, respiratory arrest, or

modes.label: Odd spots
modes.description: Occasional hits on a year digit or the start of the abbreviation OHSS in case-count sentences.
modes.example: 3 of 99 (3.0%) patients treated in the OI trial.<< OH>>SS occurred in 8 of 8

card.writes: It promotes emergency-related words (Emergency, emergencies, and Chinese terms for rescue treatment), so it adds a sense of urgent, serious outcomes.
card.plain: It lights up on the small words just before a serious complication or emergency is named.
